nodes.label: Producing services
nodes.summary: Services, schedulers and campaign jobs that request notifications. They retry, so every request carries an idempotency key.

nodes.label: Ingest API
nodes.summary: Validates, authorises and rate-limits producers, then checks the dedup store before accepting.
nodes.details: Idempotency keys matter because queues deliver at-least-once, so the same logical notification can arrive twice.

nodes.label: Dedup store
nodes.summary: TTL'd record of idempotency keys already seen, returning the previous result for repeats.

nodes.label: Orchestrator
nodes.summary: Loads preferences, device tokens and rules. Drops or delays for opt-out, quiet hours and frequency caps, and logs the reason. Renders the template.
nodes.details: APNs returns 429 for too many consecutive requests to one token, which is one reason to cap per-user frequency.

nodes.label: Preferences + tokens
nodes.summary: Per-user opt-ins and quiet hours, and device tokens with a last-seen timestamp. Stale tokens (FCM: not connected for a month) are pruned.
nodes.details: Store a timestamp with every token, delete on APNs 410 Unregistered and FCM UNREGISTERED (404).

nodes.label: Push queue (high priority)
nodes.summary: Separate queue and workers for urgent notifications (OTP, fraud) so a marketing blast cannot starve them.
nodes.details: Standard queues give at-least-once delivery and best-effort ordering, so workers must be idempotent.

nodes.label: Push queue (normal)
nodes.summary: Bulk and marketing push. Throttled to provider limits and pausable.

nodes.label: Email / SMS queues
nodes.summary: One queue per channel, so a provider outage on one channel does not stall the others.

nodes.label: Channel workers
nodes.summary: Call the provider with the right priority, TTL and collapse key. Retry with back-off on retryable errors. Never retry errors that cannot succeed.
nodes.details: APNs: do not retry BadDeviceToken, DeviceTokenNotForTopic, Forbidden, ExpiredToken, Unregistered or PayloadTooLarge. 5xx can be retried with back-off, 15 minutes after a Shutdown.

nodes.label: Dead-letter queue
nodes.summary: Messages that keep failing land here after maxReceiveCount receives, for inspection and redrive. Retention should exceed the source queue's.

nodes.label: APNs
nodes.summary: Apple's push service. HTTP/2, 4 KB payload, priority 10/5/1, apns-expiration (0 = one attempt, no storage), apns-collapse-id (≤64 bytes), one stored notification per bundle ID.

nodes.label: FCM
nodes.summary: Google's push service. TTL 0–28 days (default 4 weeks), collapse_key, normal vs high priority, Doze can delay normal-priority delivery.

nodes.label: End user (device)
nodes.summary: Receives the push, may show only the latest if several were stored while offline.

steps.caption: A service asks to notify a user, with an idempotency key so a retry cannot create a second notification.
The ingest API checks whether this key was already accepted.
New request: hand it to the orchestrator.
The orchestrator loads the user's preferences and device tokens, and checks opt-out, quiet hours and frequency caps.
An urgent message goes to the high-priority push queue so bulk traffic cannot delay it.
A channel worker dequeues it. Queues are at-least-once, so the worker records the send to stay idempotent.
For an iPhone the worker POSTs to APNs with priority 10, a short expiration and a collapse ID.
APNs delivers on a best-effort basis. Acceptance is not a delivery receipt.

flows.name: APNs says the token is dead

steps.caption: The worker sends a push to a stored token.
APNs answers 410 Unregistered: the token is no longer active for this app.
Do not retry. Remove or deactivate the token so it is never used again.
A send fails with a 5xx or Shutdown response.
These are retryable (after 15 minutes on Shutdown). 429 is retryable after a delay. Use back-off with jitter.
After maxReceiveCount failed attempts the message moves to the dead-letter queue for inspection and redrive.
A normal-priority notification is queued for bulk delivery.
It sends to FCM with a TTL (default 4 weeks, max 28 days) and a collapse_key so an older pending message is replaced.
In Doze, normal priority delivery may be delayed until the device wakes. High priority is reserved for time-sensitive, user-visible content.
